RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

Raising the panel’s gender composition without concrete evidence of bias will appear speculative and could severely harm your academic reputation and future career prospects. Academic appointments frequently hinge on non-metric criteria such as specific subfield alignment, job talk and interview dynamics, teaching philosophy, and institutional strategic needs—such as valuing her industry experience. 

Additionally, university hiring bureaucracy is notoriously slow; two weeks without post-interview feedback is normal. Follow up politely to request constructive feedback focused on professional development. If formal feedback or procedural documents later disclose overt bias or policy violations, you can consult a union or ombudsperson, but challenging the composition of the panel itself is unsubstantiated and counterproductive.
